before: Existing Taskmaster PRD describes replacing authentication with first-run local user onboarding.
after: Taskmaster PRD is replaced with a new feedback and Tauri auto-update PRD based on docs/feedback-and-update-plan.md.

before: No diagnostics helper exists for feedback submissions, and Taskmaster task 22 is pending.
after: A browser-safe diagnostics helper exists for future feedback payloads, and Taskmaster task 22 can be moved through in-progress to done after verification.

before: No Netlify feedback function exists, and Taskmaster task 26 is pending.
after: A Netlify feedback function validates feedback, verifies Turnstile, rate-limits submissions, creates GitHub issues, and Taskmaster task 26 is completed after verification.

before: No feedback submission helper exists, feedback endpoint configuration is not exported, and Taskmaster task 23 is pending.
after: A feedback helper persists drafts, builds validated payloads, submits to the configured endpoint, clears successful drafts, and Taskmaster task 23 is completed after verification.

before: No feedback modal UI exists, the feedback helper has no XMLUI window bridge, and Taskmaster task 24 is pending.
after: A feedback modal can collect and validate feedback, restore drafts, preview diagnostics, submit through the helper bridge, show success/error states, and Taskmaster task 24 is completed after verification.

before: The Tauri desktop shell does not register the updater plugin, does not create updater artifacts, and Taskmaster task 27 is pending.
after: The Tauri desktop shell registers the updater plugin, creates updater artifacts with the provided public key and update endpoint, ignores local signing key files, and Taskmaster task 27 is completed after verification.

before: The updater public key is committed directly in desktop/tauri.conf.json.
after: The updater public key is read from TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY by the desktop plugin builder, while tauri.conf.json keeps only a non-secret placeholder.

before: Settings has no Help & feedback section, no feedback enable toggle, and no way to open the feedback modal.
after: Settings exposes Help & feedback with a persisted enable toggle and Send feedback action that opens FeedbackModal outside demo mode.

before: Public-facing docs contain private-preview language, stale web/ paths, old pinned install versions, and claims that need to be checked against the current app direction.
after: Public-facing docs consistently describe the current app, app/ layout, release/install flow, privacy/security posture, and public contribution expectations.

before: Repository metadata and environment examples have not been audited for public visibility, package names, descriptions, private flags, and current configuration names.
after: Repository metadata and environment examples are accurate, publish-safe, and aligned with the public Animo project naming and configuration.

before: Code and runtime config have not been audited for stale product direction, hard-coded private assumptions, public URLs, update endpoints, diagnostics, and release-install behavior.
after: Code and runtime config match the current public-facing direction and do not contain obvious stale naming, private-preview behavior, or unsafe public defaults.

before: CI, release, changelog, update-manifest, and download-manifest automation have not been checked for public repository readiness.
after: CI and release automation are documented and configured for a public repository, with no stale private-preview assumptions in generated manifests or workflows.

before: Ignored local env files exist, including at least one real-looking provider API key and development secrets that should not survive a public-readiness pass.
after: Local env files are either removed from the working tree or reduced to safe placeholders, .gitignore continues to protect env material, and any exposed-looking keys are rotated outside the repo.

before: The landing page hero shows a hard-coded version separate from the downloads manifest, and demo links navigate in the current tab.
after: Landing and download pages read the displayed release version from the same downloads manifest, and all demo links open in a new browser tab.
